orders.reason: Progressive exertional dyspnea; brother with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35M, breathing.

The winded feeling on site has been building for about a year. Now it's every flight of stairs with a load, and he stops halfway up a ladder run that he used to do without thinking. Albuterol helps a little, using it most workdays. No fevers, no blood in sputum, no chest pain, no ankle swelling. Usual smoker's morning cough.

The real reason he called: his older brother, 37, was just diagnosed with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency after a lung workup. Their mother has emphysema too. He's worried this is the same thing.

Smoking: still about a pack a day, "down from a pack and a half some weeks."

Exam: SpO2 95% at rest. No distress. Lungs: air movement reduced at the bases, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular. No clubbing, no edema.

A/P
Progressive exertional dyspnea in a 35 y/o smoker with a brother newly diagnosed with AATD and a mother with emphysema. Needs a proper workup - pulmonology referral placed (they'll do imaging, PFTs and the AAT level/phenotype together). Continue albuterol prn. Asked him again to stop smoking; for the first time he said he'd "think hard about it." Gave quitline info and offered varenicline - wants to wait for the lung doctor's verdict.

events.reason: Progressive dyspnea; family history of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

reports.text: Technique: noncontrast CT of the chest, thin-section reconstructions. Lungs: diffuse emphysema, predominantly in the lower lobes, with a panlobular pattern and relative sparing of the upper lobes. No consolidation, nodule or mass. No pleural effusion. Airways patent. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen: both kidneys incompletely imaged, containing cysts, consistent with known polycystic kidney disease.
Acceptable and reproducible efforts. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62. FEV1 71% of predicted. FVC within normal limits. Minimal bronchodilator response.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE - OUTSIDE CONSULT LETTER
Visit date: 05/30/2023
Referred by: primary care

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Webster for shortness of breath that has gradually worsened over the past year. His 37-year-old brother was recently found to have lung disease from alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency; his mother has emphysema. He smokes about a pack a day and has since his late teens. He works construction. Medications: albuterol as needed, occasional ibuprofen. NKDA.

On examination breath sounds were reduced on both sides and the bases were hyperresonant to percussion. No wheeze, no clubbing.

CT chest today shows diffuse emphysema that is worst at the bases. Spirometry: post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 71% predicted. Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin returned at 28 mg/dL, and phenotyping shows Pi*ZZ.

Impression: severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (ZZ) with basilar panlobular emphysema and moderate airflow obstruction, in an active smoker.

Plan
1. Smoking cessation is the single most important thing he can do. We talked frankly about how fast lungs decline in ZZ smokers. Nicotine replacement or varenicline are reasonable through your office.
2. Augmentation therapy (weekly IV alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor) was discussed. We do not start it while he is smoking; we will revisit once he has quit.
3. Continue albuterol as needed for now.
4. Keep vaccines current (influenza, COVID, pneumococcal - I see PCV20 was given last fall).
5. ZZ also affects the liver: a hepatic panel yearly would be appreciated, through your office.
6. Avoid dusty work without a respirator where he can.
7. Follow-up here in one year with repeat spirometry.

Allergies: NKDA.
Pulmonology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the lung consult.

AATD, ZZ, level 28; emphysema at both bases; FEV1 71%. He's read about it online since. Understands the brother and he share it.

Smoking: the big topic. Cut to about 15 cigarettes a day the past week. Wants to try on his own first. Offered varenicline again - declines for now, worried about "weird dreams" a coworker had. Not interested in patch either. Set a loose goal of a quit date before summer ends. Augmentation therapy off the table until he quits - he knows.

Breathing same. Albuterol most workdays.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs with diminished breath sounds at bases, no wheeze. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, ZZ, with panlobular emphysema - per pulm. Hepatic panel today, then yearly.
2. Tobacco - as above, revisit monthly by text if he's willing. He said yes.
3. ADPKD - nephrology in September.
4. Albuterol prn continues.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your liver tests are normal. We'll repeat them once a year with your physical. How are the cigarettes going?

documents.title: RE: Liver tests
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good news. Cigarettes not great honestly, back to most of a pack. Still trying.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
NEPHROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit: 09/13/2023

ADPKD, one year since diagnosis. Interval: diagnosed with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and emphysema in the spring. Still smoking. No flank pain, no hematuria, no UTIs.

Home BP 120s/70s. Office BP 122/76.
Creatinine today 1.25 (1.2 last year). Urine albumin normal on your October draw.

Meds: albuterol prn. He reports using ibuprofen rarely - reminded again to avoid it.
NKDA.

Assessment: ADPKD, stable kidney function, normotensive without medication.
Plan: same - hydration, no NSAIDs, BP at home, labs yearly with PCP. Return 1 year.
Nephrology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical (rescheduled from 10/3).

35M with ADPKD (normotensive, nephrology yearly), AATD ZZ with emphysema (pulm yearly), tobacco use.

Interval: saw nephrology in Sept, creatinine 1.25, no changes. Breathing stable, albuterol most workdays. Smoking: "between half and a whole pack." Quit for 4 days in August, irritable, went back. Still declines varenicline.

NKDA. Meds: albuterol prn; ibuprofen rarely.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished at bases, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart RRR. Abdomen: palpable kidneys, nontender. Ext warm, pulses palpable. No edema.

Plan:
- Labs: CMP (includes liver tests for AATD), CBC, lipids, UACR.
- Flu and updated COVID vaccine today.
- PHQ-2 1.
- Tobacco: 4 days is a start. Door open on medication.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine at his recent level, liver tests normal, UACR normal, lipids and CBC fine. Released with comment.
